title: Customer priority scorecard and escalation triage playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We receive inconsistent escalation signals from top accounts (support tickets, account exec emails, CSM Slack pings) and lack a repeatable way to decide what becomes a roadmap priority versus a short-term mitigation. This leads to ad-hoc engineering work, missed SLAs for VIP customers, and difficulty tracking business outcomes in OKRs.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable 'Customer Priority Scorecard' that quantifies urgency and strategic value for escalations, and a corresponding 'Triage Playbook' that prescribes intake fields, ownership, timelines, and remediation/communication templates. The output will be a scoring rubric, an intake form, an escalation SLA matrix, and playbook runbooks for AMs/CSMs/Support/Eng.

Success metrics:
- 80% of top-account escalations routed to the correct owner within 4 business hours after launch.
- Reduction of unprioritized engineering interrupts from top accounts by 40% within next quarter.
- Scorecard used as primary input for 90% of roadmap reprioritization conversations for top 25 ARR accounts.

Scope: Focus initially on top 25 ARR accounts and enterprise customers in dedicated deployments. Excludes product-wide feature requests from self-serve customers (handled by standard PM triage).

Deliverables:
- Customer Priority Scorecard (spreadsheet + Confluence page) with weighted criteria: ARR impact (0-30), SLA violation severity (0-25), security/regulatory risk (0-20), strategic alignment & contract renewal status (0-15), engineering effort multiplier (negative modifier), workaround availability (positive modifier).
- Intake form (Zendesk/Confluence template + optional Slack shortcut) capturing required fields: customer, account tier, incident type, reproducible steps, logs/artifacts, exec escalation flag, desired outcome, legal/compliance note.
- Escalation SLA matrix (response & investigation SLAs per tier).
- Triage playbook runbooks for AM/CSM/Support/Eng on-call, including communication templates and temporary mitigation options (config toggles, route to fallback models).
- Integration plan with roadmap reviews and OKR cadence (how scorecard informs quarterly initiatives).

Out of scope: Automated enforcement in the Console or webhook integrations for Q1; that is a follow-on (see dependencies).
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard spreadsheet exists and populated with example data for 10 recent top-account escalations
Confluence playbook published and reviewed by PM, Support, Sales Engineering, and Legal
Intake form prototype deployed in Zendesk sandbox with fields and an actionable webhook to a triage Slack channel
SLA matrix agreed and signed off by Head of Support and Head of Customer Success
At least two simulated escalations run-through with the playbook and outcomes logged
decision_log: 2026-02-24: Agreed to weight ARR impact highest (30%) to ensure revenue-driven prioritization — decision by PM leadership and Sales ops.
2026-03-02: Chose to route intake through Zendesk with optional Slack shortcut rather than building Console integration for Q1 to accelerate launch (trade-off: limited automation).
2026-03-09: Accepted the proposed SLA tiers: Tier 1 (top 25 ARR) = 4h response / 24h investigation, Tier 2 = 8h / 72h. Support and CS approved.

2026-03-11: Decided to record 'engineering effort multiplier' as a negative modifier rather than raw score to avoid penalizing high-value complex work; engineering agreed to provide effort buckets (S/M/L/XL).
updates: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff meeting with Support, CS, Sales Eng, and Legal. Collected 18 historical ticket examples to seed scorecard.
2026-02-28 — Prototype scorecard spreadsheet v0.3 created; initial weights applied and sanity-checked on 12 cases. Feedback: increase weight for SLA violations.
2026-03-04 — Draft intake form fields agreed. Engineering requests logs/artifacts to be mandatory for escalations claiming runtime regressions.
2026-03-06 — PM tabletop run with simulated escalation: identified missing step for 'temporary traffic routing' and added a mitigation checklist for Dedicated customers.
2026-03-09 — SLA matrix finalized and signed by Support & CS leads. Legal requested an extra field for 'data residency/regulatory note' in intake form.
2026-03-12 — Playbook draft posted to Confluence for cross-functional review. Action items: ENG to scope webhook (ENG-2814), Console team to assess roadmap integration (ENG-2999).
notes: Follow-on work: automate scoring and surface top-account flags in the Console (candidate for Cycle 2026-W14).
Consider adding a lightweight customer-facing status page template for top accounts to standardize communications on multi-hour incidents.
Monitor for false positives where high scores are driven by low-effort work — adjust engineering-effort multiplier after 6 weeks of usage.
